sampling_model.design: Fixed finite family of perfect-intervention settings \(v=(S,x)\), where \(x=0\) or a unit coordinate vector in \(\mathbb R^S\).
sampling_model.units: For the statistical rung, \(m\) independent equilibrium observations are drawn in every retained setting; population identification uses the full response kernels.
sampling_model.treatment: A treatment sets every observed coordinate in \(S\) to \(x\) and preserves the remaining equations and source laws.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is needed because regimes are designed; every retained regime has \(m\) draws.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No source separation is performed. Empirical characteristic functions at \(J_m\) computable rational frequencies are compared with globally certified compact-model characteristic functions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For irreducible latent cyclic linear non-Gaussian models, observational distribution equivalence is characterized by equality of children-basis families up to a vertex permutation.
Latent directed acyclic graphs are hard-intervention equivalent exactly when their intervention-indexed augmented maximal ancestral graphs satisfy the stated skeleton and collider criteria.
The pair condition together with the covariance condition is necessary and sufficient for full recovery of a linear cyclic model from experimental means and covariances.

Proposition 5.1 states that the observational distribution together with the atomic interventional distribution for coordinate \(i\) recovers row \(i\) of the square coefficient matrix, hence its parents and causal effects.
Aligned single-target equilibrium response maps identify a latent cyclic mechanism under full target coverage, with a graph-dependent characterization when one target is missing.
Cross-cumulant tensor rank restrictions yield goodness-of-fit tests for latent linear non-Gaussian structural equation models.
Inverting graph-indexed goodness-of-fit tests yields asymptotically valid confidence sets for causal orderings in acyclic additive-error models.

body.tldr: The paper gives a sound-and-complete finite criterion for equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel sets in latent linear non-Gaussian feedback models. The exact-support theorem combines exact affine and Hall--Rado realization, a Bernoulli-diagnostic source-partition theorem, and simultaneous response matrices for one common mechanism. A new downward-closure theorem proves \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G)=\bigcup_{F\subseteq G}\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(F)\) and characterizes the zero-allowed class by a finite exact-stratum cover, while explicit sign-cell compilers decide both versions with size-dependent bit bounds. Centering and moments are absent from the population equivalence theory and remain local to the finite-variance witness and statistical subclass.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. characterize observational distributional equivalence for the zero-allowed LiNG class; existing results do not characterize equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel sets or the additional requirement that one mechanism and source tuple realize all regimes. Graphical intervention equivalence for latent acyclic models and second-order experiment-design recovery address different objects and do not supply this cyclic full-law common-mechanism criterion.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a finite coupled invariant that retains exact structural completion, lower-dimensional cancellations, invisible or merged independent sources, principal intervention responses, and common-mechanism gluing. Its downward closure must compare every exact support stratum of the source graph against a finite disjunction of exact support strata of the target graph; exact-support equality alone does not transfer monotonically.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the exact-stratum criterion using graph-generated affine and rank charts, eliminates arbitrary source laws with an admissible Bernoulli diagnostic and Laurent factorization, and identifies response slopes by rigidity of probability laws under nonzero translation. It then proves the finite union formula and downward-closed cover criterion for zero-allowed supports and compiles both relations by effective sign-condition elimination with explicit finite complexity bounds. The zero-allowed theorem matches Dai et al.'s fixed-latent observational class when \(\mathcal I=\{\varnothing\}\) and extends it to joint interventions realized by one common mechanism and source tuple.

body.related_work: Dai et al. characterize observational distributional equivalence for the zero-allowed LiNG class; existing results do not characterize equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel sets or the additional requirement that one mechanism and source tuple realize all regimes. At \(\mathcal I=\{\varnothing\}\), the new zero-allowed theorem matches their fixed-latent observational class; for larger intervention families it adds simultaneous response constraints and common-mechanism gluing. The exact-support theorem remains the stratum-level engine, while the zero-allowed result is proved by the explicit finite union \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}^{\leq}(G)=\bigcup_{F\subseteq G}\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(F)\), not by a monotonicity assertion. Zhou et al. study do-calculus invariances for latent directed acyclic graphs rather than equality of cyclic parametric response-kernel sets. Bongers et al. supply intervention-solvability semantics. Hyttinen, Eberhardt, and Hoyer characterize experiment designs for second-order full recovery, and Taeb et al. study an acyclic Gaussian latent intervention setting; neither result eliminates unrestricted non-Gaussian source laws or certifies one joint latent feedback mechanism across regimes. Sharifian et al. provide a square no-latent row-recovery comparator, while the present source-partition, downward-closure, and common-response criteria address the graph-level latent cyclic law-set problem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The population compiler is exact but intentionally exponential and uses deliberately loose real-algebraic bit bounds. It is uniform for each finite \(N\), fixed latent cardinality, and finite intervention family; it does not traverse unbounded latent cardinalities. The separate-versus-joint question still asks whether graph-generated regime-wise witness fibers can fail to share a common root and, if so, for a smallest explicit pair. The statistical theorem remains confined to the compact Laplace subclass with coefficient, inverse, edge, and scale margins.
body.honest_scope: The proved population results cover arbitrary independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources without centering or moment assumptions, arbitrary admissible algebraic cancellations, arbitrary cycles, exact support, and the zero-allowed downward closure on one fixed finite latent node set. The exact and zero-allowed criteria compare full affine response kernels under one common mechanism and source tuple; they do not claim source recovery from one observed law. Finite second moments are used only for the covariance formulation of the strict-refinement witness, and Laplace scales plus compact margins are used only for statistical certification. The new zero-allowed result matches Dai et al.'s fixed-latent observational class at the observational intervention family and supplies the additional common-mechanism joint-intervention constraints.
